ipni_publication.name: Pycnanthemum muticum (Michx.) Pers.
ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Persoon (vol. 1: preface x, paragraph 3) mentioned: Varietates praecipuae et subspecies non omissae sunt. Speciebus obscuris, aut quoad sedem dubiis, rel accuratiori indagationi subjiciendis, signa crucis seu astericsum apposui. Boivin (in Brittonia 14: 330. 1962) interpreted that * sign refers to the rank subspecies and Greek letters refer to varieties. Greuter (in Candollea 23: 90-92. 1968) concluded that the Greek lettered taxa, unless indicated as variety, are unranked and * sign refers to obscurely known species. Persoon treated most of his infrageneric names at the rank of subgenus (vide preface ix, paragraph 2 (Melius autem judicavi, eas species (nonnullis forte tamen excipiendis) ab aliis leviter in charactere aberrantes, imprimis si genus minus amplum sit, sub divisione peculiari aut subgenere, quo etiam nonnula Botanicorum recentium genera relata sunt, comprehendere, ne ultra necessitatem genera multiplicentur) and index title in vol. 1, p. 527 (Index Generum, subgenerum, nominum Familiae plantarum et synonymorum generum praecipuorum)). [See George K. Brizicky, Taxon 18(4): 646, 649. 1969]. Occasionally, Persoon used parenthetical epithets (e.g., 1: 411: ‘Combretum decandrum (album))’; he (preface p. ix) explained his usage as: ‘in parenthesi nomen quasi secundarium passim addidi, quo idea plantae forte distinctior concipi possit’. It is evident that Persoon proposed C. album and such names as alternative names. [BHL_title_id:638] [BHL_page_id:33189654]

Specific names followed by diagnoses and descriptions signed S. must be ascribed to Schumacher, those followed by Th. to Thonning; many names are followed by a diagnosis signed S. and a description signed Th. ipni_publication.name: Anthriscus Pers.
ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Persoon (vol. 1: preface x, paragraph 3) mentioned: Varietates praecipuae et subspecies non omissae sunt. Speciebus obscuris, aut quoad sedem dubiis, rel accuratiori indagationi subjiciendis, signa crucis seu astericsum apposui. Boivin (in Brittonia 14: 330. 1962) interpreted that * sign refers to the rank subspecies and Greek letters refer to varieties. Greuter (in Candollea 23: 90-92. 1968) concluded that the Greek lettered taxa, unless indicated as variety, are unranked and * sign refers to obscurely known species. Persoon treated most of his infrageneric names at the rank of subgenus (vide preface ix, paragraph 2 (Melius autem judicavi, eas species (nonnullis forte tamen excipiendis) ab aliis leviter in charactere aberrantes, imprimis si genus minus amplum sit, sub divisione peculiari aut subgenere, quo etiam nonnula Botanicorum recentium genera relata sunt, comprehendere, ne ultra necessitatem genera multiplicentur) and index title in vol. 1, p. 527 (Index Generum, subgenerum, nominum Familiae plantarum et synonymorum generum praecipuorum)). [See George K. Brizicky, Taxon 18(4): 646, 649. 1969]. Occasionally, Persoon used parenthetical epithets (e.g., 1: 411: ‘Combretum decandrum (album))’; he (preface p. ix) explained his usage as: ‘in parenthesi nomen quasi secundarium passim addidi, quo idea plantae forte distinctior concipi possit’. It is evident that Persoon proposed C. album and such names as alternative names. [BHL_title_id:638] [BHL_page_id:33189654]

ipni_publication.name: Aronia arbutifolia (L.) Pers.
ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Persoon (vol. 1: preface x, paragraph 3) mentioned: Varietates praecipuae et subspecies non omissae sunt. Speciebus obscuris, aut quoad sedem dubiis, rel accuratiori indagationi subjiciendis, signa crucis seu astericsum apposui. Boivin (in Brittonia 14: 330. 1962) interpreted that * sign refers to the rank subspecies and Greek letters refer to varieties. Greuter (in Candollea 23: 90-92. 1968) concluded that the Greek lettered taxa, unless indicated as variety, are unranked and * sign refers to obscurely known species. Persoon treated most of his infrageneric names at the rank of subgenus (vide preface ix, paragraph 2 (Melius autem judicavi, eas species (nonnullis forte tamen excipiendis) ab aliis leviter in charactere aberrantes, imprimis si genus minus amplum sit, sub divisione peculiari aut subgenere, quo etiam nonnula Botanicorum recentium genera relata sunt, comprehendere, ne ultra necessitatem genera multiplicentur) and index title in vol. 1, p. 527 (Index Generum, subgenerum, nominum Familiae plantarum et synonymorum generum praecipuorum)). [See George K. Brizicky, Taxon 18(4): 646, 649. 1969]. Occasionally, Persoon used parenthetical epithets (e.g., 1: 411: ‘Combretum decandrum (album))’; he (preface p. ix) explained his usage as: ‘in parenthesi nomen quasi secundarium passim addidi, quo idea plantae forte distinctior concipi possit’. It is evident that Persoon proposed C. album and such names as alternative names. [BHL_title_id:638] [BHL_page_id:33189654]

ipni_publication.name: Sabal minor (Jacq.) Pers.
ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Persoon (vol. 1: preface x, paragraph 3) mentioned: Varietates praecipuae et subspecies non omissae sunt. Speciebus obscuris, aut quoad sedem dubiis, rel accuratiori indagationi subjiciendis, signa crucis seu astericsum apposui. Boivin (in Brittonia 14: 330. 1962) interpreted that * sign refers to the rank subspecies and Greek letters refer to varieties. Greuter (in Candollea 23: 90-92. 1968) concluded that the Greek lettered taxa, unless indicated as variety, are unranked and * sign refers to obscurely known species. Persoon treated most of his infrageneric names at the rank of subgenus (vide preface ix, paragraph 2 (Melius autem judicavi, eas species (nonnullis forte tamen excipiendis) ab aliis leviter in charactere aberrantes, imprimis si genus minus amplum sit, sub divisione peculiari aut subgenere, quo etiam nonnula Botanicorum recentium genera relata sunt, comprehendere, ne ultra necessitatem genera multiplicentur) and index title in vol. 1, p. 527 (Index Generum, subgenerum, nominum Familiae plantarum et synonymorum generum praecipuorum)). [See George K. Brizicky, Taxon 18(4): 646, 649. 1969]. Occasionally, Persoon used parenthetical epithets (e.g., 1: 411: ‘Combretum decandrum (album))’; he (preface p. ix) explained his usage as: ‘in parenthesi nomen quasi secundarium passim addidi, quo idea plantae forte distinctior concipi possit’. It is evident that Persoon proposed C. album and such names as alternative names. [BHL_title_id:638] [BHL_page_id:33189654]

ipni_publication.name: Ficus macrophylla Pers.
ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Persoon (vol. 1: preface x, paragraph 3) mentioned: Varietates praecipuae et subspecies non omissae sunt. Speciebus obscuris, aut quoad sedem dubiis, rel accuratiori indagationi subjiciendis, signa crucis seu astericsum apposui. Boivin (in Brittonia 14: 330. 1962) interpreted that * sign refers to the rank subspecies and Greek letters refer to varieties. Greuter (in Candollea 23: 90-92. 1968) concluded that the Greek lettered taxa, unless indicated as variety, are unranked and * sign refers to obscurely known species. Persoon treated most of his infrageneric names at the rank of subgenus (vide preface ix, paragraph 2 (Melius autem judicavi, eas species (nonnullis forte tamen excipiendis) ab aliis leviter in charactere aberrantes, imprimis si genus minus amplum sit, sub divisione peculiari aut subgenere, quo etiam nonnula Botanicorum recentium genera relata sunt, comprehendere, ne ultra necessitatem genera multiplicentur) and index title in vol. 1, p. 527 (Index Generum, subgenerum, nominum Familiae plantarum et synonymorum generum praecipuorum)). [See George K. Brizicky, Taxon 18(4): 646, 649. 1969]. Occasionally, Persoon used parenthetical epithets (e.g., 1: 411: ‘Combretum decandrum (album))’; he (preface p. ix) explained his usage as: ‘in parenthesi nomen quasi secundarium passim addidi, quo idea plantae forte distinctior concipi possit’. It is evident that Persoon proposed C. album and such names as alternative names. [BHL_title_id:638] [BHL_page_id:33189654]

ipni_publication.name: Wedelia calycina Spreng.
ipni_publication.publication_issued: vols. 1-5: 1824-1828; 1: late 1824 (1825); 2: Jan-May 1825; 3: Jan-Jun 1826; 4(1 & 2): Jan-Jun 1827; 5: Jul-Aug 1828. Vol. 4 issued in two parts each with separate t.-p. and pagination. Vol. 5 is supplementary and has title: Systema vegetabilium. Editio decima sexta, curante Curtio Sprengel ...¹volumen v. sistens indicem generum, specierum et synonymorun, auctore Antonio Sprengel ... Vol. 4(2):¹Curae Posteriores; pp. 403-410: Fasciculus Plantarum Brasiliensium (by Heinrich Schott)
ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Although purporting to be ed. 16 of Linnaeus' Systema vegetabilium, this work must be attributed to Sprengel. In fact this should count as ed. 17; the real ed. 16 is that of Roemer & Schultes. Vol. 4 issued in two parts each with separate t.-p. and pagination. Vol. 5 is a supplementary vol. and has title: Systema vegetabilium. Editio decima sexta, curante Curtio Sprengel ... volumen v. sistens indicem generum, specierum et synonymorun, auctore Antonio Sprengel ...Sprengel (preface v) acknowledged contributions from several people, viz., ‘Accedit Willdenowii herbarium, cuius usque inspiciendi copiam fecit magistratus, faciunt amici. Super haec et celebranda benevolentia exterorum, maxime R. Brownii, Smithii, Balbisii, Delilii, Gussonii, Vivianii, Besseri aliorumque, qui et plantas rarissimas largiti sunt et libros praestantissimos.’ For all the new combinations or new names ascribed to the preceding authors, they are the authors. [BHL_page_id:33333952] [BHL_title_id:822]

ipni_publication.name: Pycnanthemum muticum (Michx.) Pers.
ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Persoon (vol. 1: preface x, paragraph 3) mentioned: Varietates praecipuae et subspecies non omissae sunt. Speciebus obscuris, aut quoad sedem dubiis, rel accuratiori indagationi subjiciendis, signa crucis seu astericsum apposui. Boivin (in Brittonia 14: 330. 1962) interpreted that * sign refers to the rank subspecies and Greek letters refer to varieties. Greuter (in Candollea 23: 90-92. 1968) concluded that the Greek lettered taxa, unless indicated as variety, are unranked and * sign refers to obscurely known species. Persoon treated most of his infrageneric names at the rank of subgenus (vide preface ix, paragraph 2 (Melius autem judicavi, eas species (nonnullis forte tamen excipiendis) ab aliis leviter in charactere aberrantes, imprimis si genus minus amplum sit, sub divisione peculiari aut subgenere, quo etiam nonnula Botanicorum recentium genera relata sunt, comprehendere, ne ultra necessitatem genera multiplicentur) and index title in vol. 1, p. 527 (Index Generum, subgenerum, nominum Familiae plantarum et synonymorum generum praecipuorum)). [See George K. Brizicky, Taxon 18(4): 646, 649. 1969]. Occasionally, Persoon used parenthetical epithets (e.g., 1: 411: ‘Combretum decandrum (album))’; he (preface p. ix) explained his usage as: ‘in parenthesi nomen quasi secundarium passim addidi, quo idea plantae forte distinctior concipi possit’. It is evident that Persoon proposed C. album and such names as alternative names. [BHL_title_id:638] [BHL_page_id:33189654]

ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Although purporting to be ed. 16 of Linnaeus' Systema vegetabilium, this work must be attributed to Sprengel. Vol. 5 is a supplementary vol. and has title: Systema vegetabilium. Editio decima sexta, curante Curtio Sprengel ... volumen v. sistens indicem generum, specierum et synonymorun, auctore Antonio Sprengel ...Sprengel (preface v) acknowledged contributions from several people, viz., ‘Accedit Willdenowii herbarium, cuius usque inspiciendi copiam fecit magistratus, faciunt amici. Super haec et celebranda benevolentia exterorum, maxime R. Brownii, Smithii, Balbisii, Delilii, Gussonii, Vivianii, Besseri aliorumque, qui et plantas rarissimas largiti sunt et libros praestantissimos.’ For all the new combinations or new names ascribed to the preceding authors, they are the authors. ipni_publication.name: Tephrosia virginiana (L.) Pers.
ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Persoon (vol. 1: preface x, paragraph 3) mentioned: Varietates praecipuae et subspecies non omissae sunt. Speciebus obscuris, aut quoad sedem dubiis, rel accuratiori indagationi subjiciendis, signa crucis seu astericsum apposui. Boivin (in Brittonia 14: 330. 1962) interpreted that * sign refers to the rank subspecies and Greek letters refer to varieties. Greuter (in Candollea 23: 90-92. 1968) concluded that the Greek lettered taxa, unless indicated as variety, are unranked and * sign refers to obscurely known species. Persoon treated most of his infrageneric names at the rank of subgenus (vide preface ix, paragraph 2 (Melius autem judicavi, eas species (nonnullis forte tamen excipiendis) ab aliis leviter in charactere aberrantes, imprimis si genus minus amplum sit, sub divisione peculiari aut subgenere, quo etiam nonnula Botanicorum recentium genera relata sunt, comprehendere, ne ultra necessitatem genera multiplicentur) and index title in vol. 1, p. 527 (Index Generum, subgenerum, nominum Familiae plantarum et synonymorum generum praecipuorum)). [See George K. Brizicky, Taxon 18(4): 646, 649. 1969]. Occasionally, Persoon used parenthetical epithets (e.g., 1: 411: ‘Combretum decandrum (album))’; he (preface p. ix) explained his usage as: ‘in parenthesi nomen quasi secundarium passim addidi, quo idea plantae forte distinctior concipi possit’. It is evident that Persoon proposed C. album and such names as alternative names. [BHL_title_id:638] [BHL_page_id:33189654]

ipni_publication.name: Hedeoma Pers.
ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Persoon (vol. 1: preface x, paragraph 3) mentioned: Varietates praecipuae et subspecies non omissae sunt. Speciebus obscuris, aut quoad sedem dubiis, rel accuratiori indagationi subjiciendis, signa crucis seu astericsum apposui. Boivin (in Brittonia 14: 330. 1962) interpreted that * sign refers to the rank subspecies and Greek letters refer to varieties. Greuter (in Candollea 23: 90-92. 1968) concluded that the Greek lettered taxa, unless indicated as variety, are unranked and * sign refers to obscurely known species. Persoon treated most of his infrageneric names at the rank of subgenus (vide preface ix, paragraph 2 (Melius autem judicavi, eas species (nonnullis forte tamen excipiendis) ab aliis leviter in charactere aberrantes, imprimis si genus minus amplum sit, sub divisione peculiari aut subgenere, quo etiam nonnula Botanicorum recentium genera relata sunt, comprehendere, ne ultra necessitatem genera multiplicentur) and index title in vol. 1, p. 527 (Index Generum, subgenerum, nominum Familiae plantarum et synonymorum generum praecipuorum)). [See George K. Brizicky, Taxon 18(4): 646, 649. 1969]. Occasionally, Persoon used parenthetical epithets (e.g., 1: 411: ‘Combretum decandrum (album))’; he (preface p. ix) explained his usage as: ‘in parenthesi nomen quasi secundarium passim addidi, quo idea plantae forte distinctior concipi possit’. It is evident that Persoon proposed C. album and such names as alternative names. [BHL_title_id:638] [BHL_page_id:33189654]

ipni_publication.name: Cynanchum laeve Pers.
ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Persoon (vol. 1: preface x, paragraph 3) mentioned: Varietates praecipuae et subspecies non omissae sunt. Speciebus obscuris, aut quoad sedem dubiis, rel accuratiori indagationi subjiciendis, signa crucis seu astericsum apposui. Boivin (in Brittonia 14: 330. 1962) interpreted that * sign refers to the rank subspecies and Greek letters refer to varieties. Greuter (in Candollea 23: 90-92. 1968) concluded that the Greek lettered taxa, unless indicated as variety, are unranked and * sign refers to obscurely known species. Persoon treated most of his infrageneric names at the rank of subgenus (vide preface ix, paragraph 2 (Melius autem judicavi, eas species (nonnullis forte tamen excipiendis) ab aliis leviter in charactere aberrantes, imprimis si genus minus amplum sit, sub divisione peculiari aut subgenere, quo etiam nonnula Botanicorum recentium genera relata sunt, comprehendere, ne ultra necessitatem genera multiplicentur) and index title in vol. 1, p. 527 (Index Generum, subgenerum, nominum Familiae plantarum et synonymorum generum praecipuorum)). [See George K. Brizicky, Taxon 18(4): 646, 649. 1969]. Occasionally, Persoon used parenthetical epithets (e.g., 1: 411: ‘Combretum decandrum (album))’; he (preface p. ix) explained his usage as: ‘in parenthesi nomen quasi secundarium passim addidi, quo idea plantae forte distinctior concipi possit’. It is evident that Persoon proposed C. album and such names as alternative names. [BHL_title_id:638] [BHL_page_id:33189654]
